'Quiero' can sound blunt; 'quisiera' softens the request.
drills.prompt: Make it polite using 'quisiera': Quiero una habitación individual.

focus_note: Use 'quisiera' (I would like) instead of 'quiero' (I want) to make requests sound polite. It works with a noun or an infinitive. Example: 'Quisiera un billete para Madrid' (I'd like a ticket to Madrid). 'Quería' and 'querría' are also common and polite.

lessons.title: Asking politely with quisiera
lessons.body: At a ticket desk or a hotel, 'quiero' (I want) can sound blunt. Say 'quisiera' (I would like) instead. It goes before a noun or a verb: 'Quisiera un billete para Sevilla', 'Quisiera reservar una habitación'. 'Me gustaría' (I would like) works the same way and is just as polite.
lessons.example: Quisiera una habitación doble, por favor.
lessons.example_translation: I'd like a double room, please.

lessons.title: At the station
lessons.body: To ask about trains, start with '¿A qué hora...?' (At what time...?) and use 'salir' (to leave) or 'llegar' (to arrive): '¿A qué hora sale el tren?'. A ticket is 'un billete': 'de ida' is one way, 'de ida y vuelta' is a return. Trains leave from 'el andén' (the platform).
lessons.example: ¿De qué andén sale el tren para Toledo?
lessons.example_translation: Which platform does the train to Toledo leave from?
